title: Contract risk dashboard: all contracts
audience: Renee Halvorsen, SVP, Contract Operations, and the five Regional VPs
purpose: The dashboard you designed, refreshed, with what changed overnight

fromGoal.title: Contract risk: every contract scored, and watched every morning

sections.heading: Where the portfolio stands
sections.body:
Run the full plan at every contract that rose: an odor plan at Harlow Creek, a renewal plan at Ashby Falls, cover at Red Mesa.
Harlow Creek: an odor source survey, load-out moved to mornings, the complaint calls returned and the Regional VP in front of the City Manager before the 8 December council. Ashby Falls: the Regional VP meets the new DPW Director before 2 December and the renewal plan starts now. Red Mesa: both posts covered from the West float pool on Monday and the sampling schedule given a second owner.
Contracts acted on: 3 of 300
Revenue they carry: $17.3M a year
Plans written: 3, one per site
Written for: each site, by signal

sections.heading: What changed since the last check
sections.body:
1. Overnight, 3 of the 300 contracts changed and one moved a rating: Harlow Creek WWTP in Georgia, from 2 to 3.
All 11,973 readings were read again at 06:00. Four changed, on three contracts. Harlow Creek was the contract closest to the line: its internal score went from 2.35 to 2.40 and its external score from 2.30 to 2.38, so it now rates 3, medium to high. Red Mesa in Arizona and Ashby Falls in Massachusetts changed without moving a rating. The other 297 contracts stand where they stood.

sections.heading: Ratings by region
sections.body:
1. Overnight, 3 of the 300 contracts changed and one moved a rating: Harlow Creek WWTP in Georgia, from 2 to 3.
All 11,973 readings were read again at 06:00. Four changed, on three contracts. Harlow Creek was the contract closest to the line: its internal score went from 2.35 to 2.40 and its external score from 2.30 to 2.38, so it now rates 3, medium to high. Red Mesa in Arizona and Ashby Falls in Massachusetts changed without moving a rating. The other 297 contracts stand where they stood.

2. Harlow Creek: a demand letter for 23 residents arrived at 16:42 and a sixth odor complaint was logged the same evening.
Threatened litigation goes from 2 to 4 (a demand letter is the top band) and Odor complaints from 3 to 4 (more than five in a year). The letter asks for abatement, the odor records since January 2024 and talks on compensation within 30 days, and names the City too. Five of the six complaints fall on biosolids load-out afternoons and two were never called back. The setting makes it worse: Georgia rates 4 on the state ranking (rank 46 of 50) and 11,420 homes sit within 2 miles. The contract caps liability at the annual fee but has no waiver of consequential damages.

3. Red Mesa still rates 2, but it now shows the pattern that came before five of the last seven notices of violation.
A second missed sample this quarter was recorded on 19 November, so Missed samples goes from 2 to 3 and the internal score from 1.74 to 1.78. On its own that moves nothing. Together with two operator posts open more than 60 days and overtime at 14.2% of payroll it is the combination five of the seven sites with a notice of violation since 2024 showed 8 to 12 weeks before. Both missed samples fell on weekend shifts covered on overtime by the one operator who holds the licence the contract requires.

4. Ashby Falls does not move on the scorecard, and it is the contract most likely to be lost: $7.4M a year, ending in seven months.
The Select Board agenda posted on 19 November lists "Water and sewer operations after June 2027: options including in-house operation" for 2 December, with a vote to hire a procurement adviser. The DPW Director changed in August; the NPS of 8 on file was given by her predecessor. The agreement ends 30 June 2027 with no renewal option left, and a competitor presented to the Finance Committee in October. None of this is a signal on the scorecard, so the rating stays 2. It is the same sequence as Calder Valley in 2025.

sections.heading: What needs a decision
sections.body:
Run the full plan at every contract that rose: an odor plan at Harlow Creek, a renewal plan at Ashby Falls, cover at Red Mesa (preferred)
Harlow Creek: an odor source survey, load-out moved to mornings, the complaint calls returned and the Regional VP in front of the City Manager before the 8 December council. Ashby Falls: the Regional VP meets the new DPW Director before 2 December and the renewal plan starts now. Red Mesa: both posts covered from the West float pool on Monday and the sampling schedule given a second owner.
Contracts acted on: 3 of 300 · Revenue they carry: $17.3M a year · Plans written: 3, one per site · Written for: each site, by signal
Trade-off: Three regions get work this week, one of them for a contract that still rates 2.

Plans only where a rating moved; list the rest in the Monday digest
Follow the ratings strictly: a contract that moved up gets the full plan today. A contract that rose inside its rating goes into the Monday digest.
Contracts acted on: 1 of 300 · Actions opened: 7 · Red Mesa: pattern left to run · Ashby Falls: council meets first
Trade-off: Simple to explain, since it follows the ratings. But the Ashby Falls board meets on 2 December, the same day as the review, and Red Mesa goes on with one licence holder working weekends.

Tell the owners now and decide the rest at the 2 December review
Tell the people who own each contract this morning. Take the contracts to the leadership team on 2 December and decide the plans there.
Done today: Owners told · Days used of the 30: 13 · Odor survey: not started · Disruption this week: none
Trade-off: The least work now. It uses 13 of the 30 days the letter gives, and the Ashby Falls board meets on the same day as the review.
